ddx.step1_summary:
• Chief complaint: Rapidly enlarging swelling of upper lip after eating prawn soup
• Symptom details:
  – Onset: ~30 min after meal (around 19:00)
  – Course: Progressive enlargement (“getting bigger”), throbbing, associated throat tightness / dyspnoea, dizziness
  – Severity: Worsening, patient feels unable to breathe well
  – Aggravating/alleviating factors: Triggered by prawn-containing soup; no treatment taken yet; uses salbutamol inhaler for asthma
• Past medical history: Asthma; known peanut allergy; prior similar episode of facial swelling + breathing difficulty after Chinese food (1 yr ago); hospitalised for severe allergic reaction at age 6
• Medications / allergies: Salbutamol inhaler PRN; occasional unspecified antihistamines; allergies to peanuts (now suspected shellfish). No chronic prescriptions noted.
• Family / social history: Lives with mother (present during call); no other details supplied; drinks socially (episode a year ago while intoxicated)
• Vital signs / exam findings: No formal vitals taken. Patient subjectively breathless, dizzy, audible swelling of upper lip noticed by doctor via video.
• Labs / imaging: None provided

V: Angioedema from acquired C1-INH deficiency (can present with swelling, but usually not food-triggered)
I: Cellulitis of the lip: infection could cause swelling, erythema, pain
N: Lip hemangioma or malignant neoplasm: chronic mass could enlarge but not acutely after food
D: Nutritional (niacin/B-vit) deficiency leading to cheilitis – unlikely with acute onset
I2: ACE-inhibitor–induced angioedema – drug related, produces lip swelling
C: Hereditary angioedema (C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency) – lifelong episodic swelling, often lips/throat
A: IgE-mediated anaphylaxis to shellfish (prawn) – classic rapid lip swelling, airway compromise, dizziness
Isolated allergic angioedema/oral allergy syndrome to shellfish
T: Mechanical trauma/biting of lip producing swelling
E: Hypothyroidism-related myxedema (slow, non-pitting swelling, not acute)

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: IgE-mediated anaphylaxis triggered by shellfish (prawn) allergy
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Classic timeline (minutes to <1 h after exposure), rapidly progressive lip and probable airway swelling, dyspnoea, dizziness, prior history of food-related reactions, known atopy (peanut allergy/asthma).
Could present with lip swelling without full systemic involvement; however accompanying respiratory compromise and dizziness make generalized anaphylaxis more probable.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Hereditary or acquired C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency (hereditary angioedema)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Recurrent lip/throat swelling episodes possible, but typical attacks are not precipitated by specific foods and pruritus/urticaria are absent; age 23 could fit, but prior documented food allergy argues against.
Can cause swelling, but onset is usually over hours–days, often painful and not linked to immediate food exposure.

step4_evidence.diagnosis: IgE-mediated anaphylaxis triggered by shellfish (prawn) allergy
supporting_evidence: Swelling began ~30 min after ingestion of prawn soup (typical exposure–reaction window)
Subjective throat tightness, difficulty breathing, chest discomfort
History of atopy: peanut allergy, asthma, past severe reaction requiring hospitalisation
Similar episode after Chinese food (possible hidden shellfish/peanut) a year ago
opposing_evidence: No cutaneous urticaria reported (but anaphylaxis can occur without skin signs)
No objective vitals to confirm hypotension

supporting_evidence: Localized lip swelling after food exposure
opposing_evidence: Presence of respiratory compromise and dizziness suggests systemic involvement rather than isolated angioedema

supporting_evidence: Lack of response to standard antihistamines in many cases (not yet tried here)
opposing_evidence: Attacks usually not linked to specific allergens; here clearly precipitated by prawn soup
Patient reports lifelong peanut allergy indicating IgE-mediated mechanism instead
Very rapid onset (<1 h) atypical for infection
No pain, warmth, fever, trauma described
Temporal relation to food exposure stronger for allergy
No ACE-inhibitor or any medication use mentioned
